codeReview.summary: The gateway-ssh-terminal feature implements a complete SSH server for room-based terminal access in internal/gateway/sshterm/. The implementation consists of 6 files totaling 2041 lines: types.go (config and error types), session.go (SSH session tracking with mutex-protected state), rooms.go (room manager with session tracking and limits), server.go (SSH server with WhoIs auth, PTY allocation, signal propagation), server_test.go (38 tests), and doc.go (package documentation). The SSH server authenticates via Tailscale WhoIs, routes to tmux sessions by room ID parsed from SSH username (room-<id>@<hostname>), supports PTY allocation with TERM=xterm-256color, propagates signals (SIGINT, SIGTSTP, SIGTERM, SIGQUIT, SIGKILL, SIGUSR1/2, SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGHUP), and cleanly detaches from tmux on SSH disconnect (preserving the session for reconnection). All 8 expected behaviors are implemented and tested.

issues.description: The 'exec' channel request type is rejected with req.Reply(false, nil). This means SSH exec requests (e.g., `ssh room-id@host -- command`) will fail silently. While this is acceptable for the current use case (interactive terminal only), it could be a useful future enhancement for programmatic room access. Not blocking.

In handleConn, the SSH handshake uses ssh.NewServerConn which takes ownership of the net.Conn. If WhoIs succeeds but the SSH handshake fails, the connection is properly closed via defer sshConn.Close(). However, if WhoIs succeeds and the room is not found (line 189), the function returns without sending any error message to the client — the connection just closes. A more user-friendly approach would be to write an error message before closing. This is minor since SSH clients will see 'connection closed by remote'.

The shell handler uses exec.Command (not CommandContext) intentionally — the comment explains that context cancellation shouldn't kill the tmux process. However, the cmd.Wait() goroutine (line 290) will block indefinitely if the tmux process hangs. The deferred cleanup has a 5-second timeout with Process.Kill fallback, which is good, but the cmd.Wait goroutine itself may leak if Kill doesn't work. In practice this is extremely unlikely with tmux.

DefaultSSHServerConfig sets MaxSessions to 10. The comment on MaxSessions says 'Zero means unlimited', but the default is 10, not 0. This is a sensible default (prevents resource exhaustion), but the documentation could be clearer about why 10 was chosen.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SSH server uses NoClientAuth: true in ssh.ServerConfig because authentication is handled entirely by Tailscale WhoIs identity verification. This means the SSH server relies on the tsnet listener to only accept tailnet connections. If the SSH server is ever exposed on a non-tailnet listener (e.g., in dev mode without WhoIs), it would accept unauthenticated connections. This is documented in the code but worth noting as a security consideration.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: internal/gateway/sshterm/server.go:95 — ssh.ServerConfig{NoClientAuth: true} with comment 'Authentication is via Tailscale WhoIs'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SSH terminal reuses the same RoomManager pattern from the web terminal (rooms.go has the same Register/Unregister/AddSession/RemoveSession API shape as the webterm hub). Both terminal access methods (web and SSH) share the concept of room-based session routing with connection limits. This is a good consistency pattern.

summary: PASS. The gateway-ssh-terminal feature is a thorough implementation of SSH-based room terminal access. 38 tests cover all key behaviors: WhoIs authentication, room routing via SSH username, PTY allocation with TERM environment, signal propagation (9 signal types), clean tmux detach on disconnect, session persistence, connection limiting, and concurrent session handling. The code follows project conventions: mutex-protected state, atomic operations for server lifecycle, proper error types (RoomNotFoundError, IdentityRejectedError, SessionLimitError), and structured logging with zerolog. The implementation correctly uses exec.Command (not CommandContext) to ensure tmux sessions survive SSH disconnect. The RoomManager provides proper session tracking with limits. Four non-blocking issues noted: (1) exec requests are rejected silently, (2) room-not-found gives no client feedback, (3) cmd.Wait could theoretically leak on hung tmux, (4) MaxSessions default documentation could be clearer. All are minor robustness/convenience concerns, not correctness bugs.
